AS.name: Rocks and minerals and their exploitation

subtopics.name: Formation of rocks
objectives: describe and interpret the rock cycle
state and explain the formation and characteristics of named igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks

subtopics.name: Extraction of rocks and minerals from the Earth
objectives: describe the following methods of extraction of rocks and minerals from the Earth: - surface mining - subsurface mining
discuss the factors that affect the decision to extract rocks and minerals

subtopics.name: Impact of rock and mineral extraction
objectives: describe and explain the environmental, economic and social impacts of rock and mineral extraction

subtopics.name: Managing the impact of rock and mineral extraction
objectives: describe and evaluate strategies for restoring landscapes damaged by rock and mineral extraction

subtopics.name: Sustainable use of rocks and minerals
objectives: define sustainable resource and sustainable development
describe and evaluate strategies for the sustainable use of rocks and minerals Case study:
Study the development, impact and management of a mine including land restoration after the mine has closed.

subtopics.name: Fossil fuel formation
objectives: describe the formation of the fossil fuels: coal, oil and gas

subtopics.name: Energy resources and the generation of electricity
objectives: classify the following energy resources as non- renewable or renewable:
fossil fuels, nuclear power, biofuels, geothermal power, hydro-electric power, tidal power, wave power, solar power, wind power
describe how each of these energy resources is used to generate electricity
describe the environmental, economic and social advantages and disadvantages of each of these energy resources

subtopics.name: Energy demand
objectives: describe and explain the factors affecting the demand for energy

subtopics.name: Conservation and management of energy resources
objectives: describe and explain strategies for the efficient management of energy resources
research and development of new energy resources

subtopics.name: Impact of oil pollution
objectives: describe the causes and impacts of oil pollution on marine and coastal ecosystems

subtopics.name: Management of oil pollution
objectives: discuss strategies for reducing oil spills in marine and coastal ecosystems
discuss strategies for minimising the impacts of oil spills on the marine and coastal ecosystems Case study:
Study the impact and management of an oil pollution event.

subtopics.name: Soil composition
objectives: describe and explain the composition of soils

subtopics.name: Soils for plant growth
objectives: describe soils as a medium for plant growth
describe the differences between a sandy and clay soil

subtopics.name: Agriculture types
objectives: describe the different types of agriculture

subtopics.name: Increasing agricultural yields
objectives: describe techniques used to increase agricultural yields

subtopics.name: Impact of agriculture
objectives: describe and explain the impact of agricultural practices on the environment and people

subtopics.name: Causes and impacts of soil erosion
objectives: describe the causes of soil erosion
describe and explain the impacts of soil erosion

subtopics.name: Managing soil erosion
objectives: describe and explain strategies to reduce soil erosion

subtopics.name: Sustainable agriculture
objectives: describe and explain strategies for sustainable agriculture Case study:
Study an example where agriculture has had severe environmental consequences including soil erosion and strategies for the conservation of the soil.

subtopics.name: Global water distribution
objectives: describe the distribution of the Earth's water

subtopics.name: The water cycle
objectives: describe and interpret the water cycle

subtopics.name: Water supply
objectives: describe the sources of fresh water used by people

subtopics.name: Water usage
objectives: describe the different ways in which fresh water can be used

subtopics.name: Water quality and availability
objectives: compare the availability of safe drinking water (potable water) in different parts of the world

subtopics.name: Multipurpose dam projects
objectives: describe and evaluate multipurpose dam projects

subtopics.name: Water pollution and its sources
objectives: describe the sources of water pollution

subtopics.name: Impact of water pollution
objectives: describe and explain the impact of pollution of fresh water on people and on the environment

subtopics.name: Managing pollution of fresh water
objectives: describe and explain strategies for improving water quality

subtopics.name: Managing water-related disease
objectives: describe the life cycle of the malaria parasite
describe and evaluate strategies to control malaria
describe strategies to control cholera Case studies:
Study the impact of a named multipurpose dam scheme.
Study the causes, impact and management of pollution in a named body of water.

subtopics.name: Oceans as a resource
objectives: outline the resource potential of the oceans

subtopics.name: World fisheries
objectives: outline the distribution of major ocean currents
explain the distribution of major marine fish populations
describe the El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) phenomenon and its effects on fisheries along the Pacific coast of South America

subtopics.name: Impact of exploitation of the oceans
objectives: describe and explain the impact of exploitation of fisheries
describe how farming of marine species reduces the exploitation of fisheries

subtopics.name: Management of the harvesting of marine species
objectives: describe, explain and evaluate strategies for management of the harvesting of marine species Case studies:
Study the resource potential, exploitation, impact and management of a marine fishery.
Study an example of farming of marine species, including the source of food, pollution from waste and impact on the natural habitat.

subtopics.name: Earthquakes and volcanoes
objectives: describe the structure of the Earth
describe and explain the distribution and causes of earthquakes and volcanoes
understand magnitude and the Richter scale

subtopics.name: Tropical cyclones
objectives: describe and explain the distribution and causes of tropical cyclones (storms, hurricanes and typhoons)

subtopics.name: Flooding
objectives: describe and explain the causes of flooding

subtopics.name: Drought
objectives: describe and explain the causes of drought

subtopics.name: The impacts of natural hazards
objectives: describe and explain the impacts of natural hazards on people and the environment

subtopics.name: Managing the impacts of natural hazards
objectives: describe and evaluate the strategies for managing the impacts of natural hazards before, during and after an event

subtopics.name: Opportunities presented by natural hazards
objectives: describe and explain the opportunities presented by natural hazards to people Case studies:
Compare and contrast the strategies for managing the impacts of tectonic events between a named more economically developed country (MEDC) and a named less economically developed country (LEDC).
Study the strategies for managing the impacts of a tropical storm or flood or drought.

subtopics.name: The atmosphere
objectives: describe the structure and composition of the atmosphere
describe the natural greenhouse effect

subtopics.name: Atmospheric pollution and its causes
objectives: describe and explain the causes of atmospheric pollution, with reference to: - smog - acid rain - ozone layer depletion - enhanced greenhouse effect

subtopics.name: Impact of atmospheric pollution
objectives: describe and explain the impact of atmospheric pollution

subtopics.name: Managing atmospheric pollution
objectives: describe and explain the strategies used by individuals, governments and the international community to reduce the effects of atmospheric pollution Case study:
Study the causes, impact and management of a specific example of atmospheric pollution.

subtopics.name: Human population distribution and density
objectives: identify where people live in the world

subtopics.name: Changes in population size
objectives: describe and explain the growth curve of populations
describe and explain the changes in human populations

subtopics.name: Population structure
objectives: describe population structure in MEDCs and LEDCs

subtopics.name: Managing human population size
objectives: evaluate strategies for managing human population size Case study:
Study the strategies a named country or region has used to manage population size.

subtopics.name: Ecosystems
objectives: define the terms ecosystem, population, community, habitat and niche
describe the biotic (living) and abiotic (non- living) components of an ecosystem
describe biotic interactions
describe the process of photosynthesis
describe energy flow using food chains, food webs and trophic levels
describe and explain ecological pyramids based on numbers and energy
describe the process of respiration
describe the carbon cycle

subtopics.name: Ecosystems under threat
objectives: describe and explain causes and impacts of habitat loss

subtopics.name: Deforestation
objectives: describe and explain the causes and impacts of deforestation

subtopics.name: Managing forests
objectives: describe and explain the need for the sustainable management of forests

subtopics.name: Measuring and managing biodiversity
objectives: describe and evaluate methods for estimating biodiversity
apply sampling techniques to unfamiliar situations
evaluate national and international strategies for conserving the biodiversity and genetic resources of natural ecosystems Case studies:
Study the causes and impacts of deforestation in a named area.
Study the conservation of a named species.
Study a named biosphere reserve. Gathering of data
formulate aims and hypotheses

design questionnaires that can be oral or written to gain information from an individual or a group of individuals (consideration should be given to factors influencing the successful design of questionnaires, e.g. layout, format of questions, the appropriate wording of questions and the number of questions. The practical considerations of conducting a questionnaire, e.g. the sampling methods, pilot survey and location of survey should also be discussed)
design a simple experiment using suitable controls
understand and evaluate random and systematic sampling techniques. Mathematical requirements Calculators may be used in all parts of the examination.
add, subtract, multiply and divide
use averages, decimals, fractions, percentages, ratios and reciprocals
understand the terms mean and range
use standard notation, including both positive and negative indices
understand significant figures and use them appropriately
recognise and use direct and inverse proportion
draw tables, charts and graphs from given data
interpret charts and graphs
determine the gradient and intercept of a graph
select suitable scales and axes for graphs
make approximate evaluations of numerical expressions
understand the meaning of angle, curve, circle, radius, diameter, area, circumference, square, rectangle and diagonal
understand map scale and the use of the scale line.
